requirements.statement: After a Debug pass, the next Exercise pass covers only the representative criterion of each cause that pass addressed (plus any F-1 evidence-gap re-capture). No other open criterion is exercised or re-judged. Must pass.

The Judge groups build-defect criteria by shared root cause: every build-defect criterion carries one cause key, same-cause criteria share a key. Workflow records each cause (key, members, representative) in verification-state.json and shows it in verification-report.md. Must pass.

Debug fixes each cause once, from one gap per cause rather than one per criterion. Independent causes may be fixed in parallel; whether to is an engineering choice. Not must-pass. TRD uses one app-debugger per iteration (D8, recorded OWNER-CALL).

A cause with many members (e.g. 20 criteria) is re-checked in the inner loop through exactly one representative. When it passes, the cause is closed and other members are left for the end-of-run regression pass, not re-checked in the inner loop. Must pass.
Criteria of a cause the last Debug pass did not address stay open and untouched: not exercised or re-judged, last verdict stands. Must pass.

A check-derived criterion (derivation: check:<skill>, e.g. design comparison) takes part in the inner loop only as its cause's representative; a non-check-derived member is chosen whenever the cause has one.

A targeted unit test or Playwright spec may run as a fast pre-check before the representative is re-captured. A failing pre-check means no re-capture that iteration. A passing pre-check never settles a criterion met; only its own judged evidence does. Must pass.
The inner loop stays bounded by the existing iteration cap and stalled rule; the stalled rule counts closed causes as progress as well as closed criteria. Must pass.

One headless fixture run (fixtures environment in verification.md) seeded with two causes over at least six criteria, one fixed and one not, produces verification-state.json whose second iteration exercised only the fixed cause's representative.
Tests pass; unit coverage at least 60% and integration at least 50% where integration applies.
Every new input is validated where it enters: the three new decideNext inputs, the Judge output, and the other new inputs.

open_questions: OQ-1 (TRD; investigation OQ-1): Until roadmap item 3 lands, how are a closed cause's other members re-checked? Assumed: one confirmation pass over only those members at exit, outside the cap, no Debug after it (D15). Wrong if: item 3 arrives first and D15 is built then deleted.

OQ-2 (TRD; investigation OQ-2): Does a resume or /verify-build fix round keep the previous invocation's targeting? Assumed: no; its first iteration walks the whole open set (D18). Wrong if: a resume re-exercises criteria a targeted run would skip.

OQ-4 (TRD; investigation OQ-4): A representative that now fails under a different cause key: does its old cause close? Assumed: yes; old cause closes, members await, representative joins the new cause (D4). Wrong if: a cause closes without being fixed; TR1's confirmation pass catches it.

OQ-5 (TRD only): A representative that becomes an evidence gap, not_verifiable or unbuilt: what happens to its cause? Assumed: cause stays open, takes a new representative, exercised next iteration without another Debug pass (D4, pendingConfirmation). Source does not say.
OQ-6 (TRD only): Debug reports a cause unbuilt: is every member unbuilt, or only the representative? Assumed: every member (D9). Changes only the report's unbuilt count, not the outcome.

OQ-7 (TRD only): Should causeGroups live in the lib, as investigation Decision 2 says? Assumed: no; it lives only in the workflow, its only consumer (D3). Wrong if: a later command must regroup from a state file.

OQ-8 (TRD only): Should the cause-key format be stricter or looser than ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$? Assumed: that pattern; Judge is told the format. Wrong if: grouping silently degrades; the fallback is logged.

OQ-9 (TRD; investigation OQ-3 renumbered): Should independent causes be fixed by parallel Debug agents? Assumed: no; one app-debugger per iteration fixes every cause (D8, NG8). PM says may, so this is an engineering OWNER-CALL, not a scope change. Revisit if fixture runs show Debug dominating an iteration.
OQ-3 (investigation only, not carried into TRD as OQ-3; removed in TRD v1.1.0): How many Debug agents may run in parallel? Assumed: one per iteration (TRD D8, OWNER-CALL).
